deep.reconstruction:
The page has two unrelated parts: (A) lemniscatic theta-type functions, and (B) a numerical exclusion sieve testing whether N = 11539097 is prime. Part B continues on the next folio ('Explorare 11539097 an sit primus').

(A) LEMNISCATIC FUNCTIONS. Notation: ϖ = 2∫_0^1 dt/√(1-t^4) = 2.62205..., Gauss's lemniscate constant. Π is the entire numerator of sin lemn, sl z = Π(z)/(denominator). Its Taylor series contains only the powers z^{4k+1}, so Π(iz) = iΠ(z); it is essentially the Weierstrass σ of the square lattice. 𝔓 is the 'theta-normalised' version of Π.

Line 1: Π(xϖ) = 𝔓(xϖ)·e^{πx²/2}. In other words 𝔓(z) = Π(z)·exp(-π z²/(2ϖ²)).

Line 2: put ixϖ for xϖ. Then Π(ixϖ) = 𝔓(ixϖ)·e^{-πx²/2}. By the symmetry Π(iz) = iΠ(z) this also equals i·𝔓(xϖ)·e^{πx²/2}.

Line 3 (comparing the two): 𝔓(ixϖ) = i·𝔓(xϖ)·e^{πx²}.

Line 4, likewise for the denominator 𝔔 (only powers z^{4k}, so even under z → iz): 𝔔(ixϖ) = 𝔔(xϖ)·e^{πx²}.

Lines 5–6, for the companion pair p, q (numerator and denominator of cl): p(ixϖ) = q(xϖ)e^{πx²} and q(ixϖ) = p(xϖ)e^{πx²}. A first attempt 'p(ixϖ) = √𝔔 ...' is struck out. These lines are consistent with cl(iz) = 1/cl(z), and the exponential factors match.

This is the τ = i case of the imaginary (Jacobi) transformation of theta functions. Once the factor exp(-πz²/2ϖ²) is removed, the four functions transform into each other up to the single multiplier e^{πx²}.

Fragment '½p⁴ - ½q⁴': an unfinished quartic relation among the four functions. It cannot be reconstructed.

Integral: φ = ∫dx/√(1-x⁴). Put x = P/Q. Then dx = (QdP - PdQ)/Q² and √(1-x⁴) = √(Q⁴-P⁴)/Q², so dφ = (QdP - PdQ)/√(Q⁴-P⁴). This is correct.

Gauss then imposes the normalisation Q⁴ + P⁴ = 1. Then:
- Q³dQ + P³dP = 0, so dQ = -P³dP/Q³.
- QdP - PdQ = QdP + P⁴dP/Q³ = (Q⁴+P⁴)dP/Q³ = dP/Q³.
- Q⁴ - P⁴ = 1 - 2P⁴.
- Hence dφ = dP / [ (1-P⁴)^{3/4} √(1-2P⁴) ].

The manuscript's final form is written 'dP / √(1-2P⁴) : √(1-P⁴)'.

Series at the bottom: x·e^{-πx²/(2ϖ²)} is the leading behaviour of 𝔓. Gauss writes:
- 𝔓φ = φ - (π/ϖ²)φ³ + ...
- its inversion φ = x + (π/ϖ²)x³ + ...
- 𝔔 = 1 - πP²/ϖ² + ...
These are the first correction terms from the Gaussian factor.

(B) PRIMALITY SIEVE FOR N = 11539097, via N = x² + 88y². 88 is one of Euler's idoneal numbers, so N is prime iff it has exactly one such representation, with gcd(x, 88y) = 1.

Bound and residue mod 11:
- 3396² = 11532816 < N < 3397² = 11539609, so x < 3396.
- N ≡ 9 (mod 11), so x ≡ ±3 (mod 11).
- That leaves about 2·3396/11 ≈ 618 candidates; '(618' is written. Requiring x odd halves this to 309.

Powers of 2: N ≡ 25 (mod 64), and 88y² ≡ 0, 32 or 24 (mod 64). Hence x² ≡ 1, 25 or 57 (mod 64), so x ≡ ±1, ±5, ±11 (mod 32). The page gives:
- the lists '1,5,11' (allowed) and '3,7,13,15' (excluded);
- 'Excl. ±3,7 (16)' and '±15 (32)';
- the explicit check '25 - 9 = 16 ≡ 88y² (32)', reduced to '2 ≡ 11y² (mod 4)', which is impossible.

Odd primes: x is excluded when (N - x²)/88 is a non-residue mod p.
- mod 3: x ≡ 0 excluded.
- mod 5: x ≡ ±1 excluded.
- mod 7: 'excl. 0,2,5'.
- mod 13: allowed '1.5.6'; excluded '0,2,3,4,9,10,11'. Gauss struck 12, which is correct since 12 ≡ -1 is allowed.
- mod 17: heading '3.4.5.7'; excluded column 3,4,5,7,10,12,13,14.

Candidate counts in the right column: 309, (232?), 217, 145, 87. The last two steps match the ratios 2/3 and 3/5.

Combined tables:
- mod 22: x ≡ 3, 19.
- mod 66: x ≡ 19, 25, 41, 47.
- mod 330: x ≡ ±25, ±47, ±85, ±107, ±113, ±157.
- 3630 = 11·330 is the next combined modulus.

The congruences 1+k+10n ≡ 15, k+5n ≡ 7, 3k+15n ≡ 5 (mod 16) are consistent, since 3·7 = 21 ≡ 5. They belong to a parametrisation of the candidates. Scattered numbers (256, 153, 1493, 1567, ...) are side computations.
errors: The final form of the transformed integrand is written as dP/√(1-2P⁴) : √(1-P⁴). Under Q⁴+P⁴=1 the correct result is dP/((1-P⁴)^{3/4}√(1-2P⁴)), i.e. Q³ = (1-P⁴)^{3/4}, not √(1-P⁴). This is either a slip or an ambiguous notation.

Series coefficients: if 𝔓(z) = Π(z)e^{-πz²/(2ϖ²)} with Π(z) = z + O(z⁵), as line 1 and the fraction x/e^{½xxπ/ϖϖ} imply, then 𝔓φ = φ - (π/(2ϖ²))φ³ + ... and 𝔔 = 1 - πφ²/(2ϖ²) + .... As written, π/ϖϖ lacks the factor 1/2, unless a ½ is hidden in the handwriting.

Candidate counts: halving 309 by the mod-16 exclusion should give ≈154.5. That value is in fact written ('154½') in the middle column, so the 232 in the right column is either a misreading or refers to a different stage.
Minor: the first attempt for p(ixϖ) involving √𝔔 is struck out; the corrected line is right.

results.what: 𝔓(ixϖ) = i𝔓(xϖ)e^{πx²}, 𝔔(ixϖ) = 𝔔(xϖ)e^{πx²}, p(ixϖ) = q(xϖ)e^{πx²}, q(ixϖ) = p(xϖ)e^{πx²}, where 𝔓 = Π·exp(-πz²/2ϖ²) is the theta-normalised lemniscatic numerator.
results.modern_name: Imaginary (τ→-1/τ) transformation of theta functions at τ=i; quasi-periodicity/σ-to-θ normalisation for the square lattice.
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (1828–29) for the general theta transformation; Gauss's lemniscatic work c. 1798–1800 (published in Werke III, 1866).

results.what: Substitution x = P/Q turning dx/√(1-x⁴) into (QdP-PdQ)/√(Q⁴-P⁴), with normalisation P⁴+Q⁴=1.
results.modern_name: Change of variables in the lemniscatic elliptic integral (homogeneous coordinates on a Fermat-type quartic).

results.what: Primality test for 11539097 via representations as x²+88y², with exclusion of residue classes modulo 2^k, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and combined tables mod 22, 66, 330.
results.modern_name: Euler's idoneal-number primality criterion combined with Gauss's method of exclusion (sieve).
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (idoneal numbers, 1770s); Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae art. 303, 319–334 (1801).

deep.surprise_reason: The lemniscatic theta normalisation and its transformation under z→iz are documented in Gauss's lemniscate notes (Werke III). The exclusion method with idoneal numbers is in the Disquisitiones. The page is a worked application and a scratch derivation, not a new result.
